subsections: League's acceptance and withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan
Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: Which development immediately preceded the Muslim League's withdrawal from its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan?
o: The formation of the Interim Government in August 1947
The announcement of the Radcliffe Award
accepted.x: On 10 July 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru stated that Congress could modify the scheme through its majority in the Constituent Assembly. This prompted Jinnah and the League to withdraw their acceptance.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the immediate trigger from later constitutional events.
accepted.sec: League's acceptance and withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan

accepted.s: Direct Action Day, observed on 16 August 1946, is associated with the
accepted.x: The Muslim League observed 16 August 1946 as Direct Action Day, which resulted in the Great Calcutta Killings. The violence later spread to Noakhali, Bihar and parts of north India.
accepted.tq: Match the exact date with the well-known event associated with it.
accepted.sec: League's acceptance and withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan

accepted.s: Mahatma Gandhi undertook a peace march in Noakhali during the period
accepted.x: Gandhi walked from village to village in Noakhali from November 1946 to March 1947 to promote peace, though he could not stop the violence completely.
accepted.tq: Use the narrow date range to discriminate between similar phases of the national movement.
accepted.sec: League's acceptance and withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan

accepted.s: In the elections of 1945–46, the Muslim League won all the Muslim seats in the
accepted.x: The Muslim League won all 30 Muslim seats in the Central Legislative Assembly and most Muslim seats in the provincial elections.
accepted.tq: Identify the level of legislature and the exact numerical result instead of generalising the electoral success.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations regarding provincial ministries after the 1945–46 elections is correct?
o: League—Bengal under H.S. Suhrawardy; Congress—most provinces including NWFP
Congress—Punjab under Khizr Hayat Khan without coalition support; League—NWFP
accepted.x: The Muslim League formed ministries in Bengal under H.S. Suhrawardy and in Sindh. Congress formed ministries in most provinces, including NWFP.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure person–province pair and eliminate the reversed combinations.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: The Punjab ministry formed after the 1945–46 elections was a coalition of the
accepted.x: Punjab had a Unionist–Congress–Akali coalition ministry under Khizr Hayat Khan.
accepted.tq: Test coalition composition directly, using nearby political organisations as confusable distractors.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: Who became the premier of the Congress ministry in Madras in 1946?
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the premier of the Congress ministry in Madras in 1946. Congress won almost all the Andhra seats.
accepted.tq: Use the person–province association, a standard regional-history recall pattern.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the elections of 1945–46:
1. Congress swept the general or non-Muslim seats.
2. The Muslim League won most Muslim seats in the provinces.
3. The Communists suffered a heavy defeat after having cooperated with the British war effort.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Congress dominated the general seats, the League dominated Muslim seats, and the Communists performed poorly in the elections.
accepted.tq: Check each electoral trend separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: How many seats did the Congress win out of the 296 British Indian seats in the Constituent Assembly elections of July 1946?
accepted.x: In the Constituent Assembly elections, Congress won 208 of the 296 British Indian seats, while the Muslim League won 73 and other groups won 15.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical distribution and reject the smaller figures belonging to other groups.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: The slogan “Divide and Quit” was adopted by the Muslim League at its Karachi session held in
accepted.x: The Muslim League adopted the slogan “Divide and Quit” at its Karachi session in December 1943.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the slogan's year from the better-known Quit India period.
accepted.sec: Provincial and Constituent Assembly elections after the war

accepted.s: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress on 15 August 1947?
accepted.x: J.B. Kripalani was the Congress President at the time of Indian independence.
accepted.tq: Separate the office of Congress President from the offices of Prime Minister and Governor-General.

accepted.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 received the Royal Assent on
accepted.x: The Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947. It came into effect on 15 August 1947.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the date of Royal Assent and the date on which the Act became effective.

accepted.s: Which of the following was a consequence of the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: All princely states were automatically made independent republics
The Government of India Act, 1935 ceased to operate until new constitutions were framed
India and Pakistan became two independent dominions
The office of the Governor-General was abolished immediately
accepted.x: The Act created the two independent dominions of India and Pakistan. It allowed the Government of India Act, 1935 to operate until new constitutions were framed and did not make princely states automatically independent.
accepted.tq: Identify the legally precise consequence while rejecting absolute statements about princely states and constitutional continuity.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. The two dominions had the right to secede from the Commonwealth.
2. Paramountcy over the princely states lapsed.
3. The office of the Secretary of State for India was abolished.
4. The armed forces were divided between India and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe provisions or consequences of the Act. Paramountcy lapsed, the armed forces were divided, the Secretary of State's office was abolished, and both dominions could secede from the Commonwealth.
accepted.tq: Verify each constitutional consequence before choosing the complete combination.

accepted.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the princely states were given the option to
o: form a single federation under the British Crown
accede to either India or Pakistan
accepted.x: With the lapse of paramountcy, the 565 princely states were free to accede to India or Pakistan. Independence for the princely states was not the intended constitutional arrangement.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal effect of lapse of paramountcy to the position of princely states.

accepted.s: Who chaired both the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions in 1947?
accepted.x: Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer unfamiliar with Indian conditions, chaired both Boundary Commissions.
accepted.tq: Use the person–institution association and distinguish the boundary chairman from the Viceroy.

accepted.s: The Radcliffe Award announcing the partition boundaries was published on
accepted.x: Although independence took place on 15 August 1947, the Radcliffe Award was announced two days later, on 17 August 1947.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the boundary announcement date from the date of independence.

accepted.s: Referendums were held in which of the following areas to decide their accession at the time of partition?
o: Bengal and Assam as a whole
accepted.x: Referendums were held in the North-West Frontier Province and Sylhet. NWFP joined Pakistan, while Sylhet joined East Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Remember the exclusive pair of referendum areas and distinguish them from provinces decided by assemblies.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the method used to decide its partition or accession?
o: Punjab — decision by the British Parliament alone
NWFP — decision by its own assembly
accepted.x: Sylhet's accession was decided by referendum. Sindh's own assembly decided, NWFP held a referendum, and Punjab was divided through votes of its assembly members in separate parts.
accepted.tq: Find the one accurate province–method pair among reversed decision procedures.

accepted.s: The Cripps Mission reached Delhi on
accepted.x: Sir Stafford Cripps reached Delhi on 23 March 1942. The mission was sent by Churchill under pressure from Roosevelt and Chiang Kai-shek after Japan's advance.
accepted.tq: Use the exact arrival date to separate the mission from the later Quit India Movement.

accepted.s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the
o: Labour Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
Liberal Party and Wavell's Executive Council
Communist Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
accepted.x: Cripps was a Labour member of Churchill's War Cabinet. Churchill sent him to India in 1942 under international and military pressure.
accepted.tq: Test the exact party and cabinet association instead of relying on the person's later political reputation.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the proposals of the Cripps Mission?
o: The right of a province or princely state to stay out
A Constituent Assembly after the war
Dominion status for India after the war
Immediate transfer of complete power to an independent Indian government
accepted.x: The Cripps proposals offered dominion status after the war, not immediate complete independence or immediate transfer of full power. They also proposed a Constituent Assembly and allowed provinces or princely states to stay out.
accepted.tq: Look for the proposal that changes a delayed constitutional offer into immediate transfer of power.

accepted.s: Under the Cripps proposals, defence was to remain with the British
o: until the end of the war
only until the Constituent Assembly was elected before the war
until the partition of India in 1947
accepted.x: The Cripps proposals kept defence under British control until the end of the war. This was one reason the offer did not satisfy Indian political opinion.
accepted.tq: Apply the time limitation in the proposal rather than choosing an absolute or post-1947 alternative.

accepted.s: The failure of the Cripps Mission contributed directly to the launching of the
accepted.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission, which did not provide immediate power to Indian leaders, contributed to the decision to launch the Quit India Movement.
accepted.tq: Trace the immediate political consequence rather than selecting an earlier mass movement.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the principal reactions to the Cripps proposals?
o: Congress rejected them for lack of immediate power and risk of Balkanisation; Churchill considered them too radical
Congress rejected them only because they promised full independence after the war
Congress accepted them as immediate independence and Churchill regarded them as too conservative
Both Congress and Churchill accepted them without reservation
accepted.x: Congress objected to the absence of immediate power and the possibility of Balkanisation. Churchill considered the proposals too radical, while many Indians regarded them as too conservative.
accepted.tq: Compare the reasons for rejection from both sides and eliminate the reversed reactions.
